research_rationale:
EO 10977 (John F. Kennedy; signed 1961-12-04; 26 FR 11471, published 1961-12-05) establishes the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal. Section 1 establishes it for members of the Armed Forces who after July 1, 1958 (a) participate as members of United States military units in a military operation in which personnel of any military department participate in significant numbers in the opinion of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and (b) encounter foreign armed opposition incident to that participation or are placed where, in the Joint Chiefs' opinion, hostile action by foreign armed forces was imminent. Section 2 sets the design (approved by the Secretary of Defense), the awarding officials (the Secretary of the military department concerned, and, for the Coast Guard, the Secretary named in the order) and uniform regulations by the Secretary of Defense. Section 3 limits the medal to operations for which no other United States campaign medal is approved and to one medal per person with devices for later operations. Section 4 allows posthumous award. The held text is the official Federal Register text layer for PDF page 3 of the 1961-12-05 issue (location confidence high); the six dossier scopes cover sections 1(a), 1(b), 1 (lead-in), 2, 3 and 4, and the authority recital and signature block are not operative text. Later events read from held texts: EO 11382 section 13(3) (signed 1967-11-28) struck 'Secretary of the Treasury' and inserted 'Secretary of Transportation'; EO 13286 section 72 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) struck 'the Secretary of Transportation' in section 2 and inserted 'the Secretary of Homeland Security'. Three later medal orders provide, notwithstanding section 3, that members who qualified for the medal for service in a named theater remain qualified and may take the later medal instead: EO 11231 section 2 (Vietnam Service Medal, signed 1965-07-08), EO 13154 section 2 (Kosovo Campaign Medal, signed 2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (Global War on Terrorism Medals, signed 2003-03-12). None ends the order. The dossier also lists an EO 12977 entry, but the amendment it quotes is section 72 of EO 13286 (68 FR 10619), a queue file mislabelled with the EO 12977 number; EO 13286 is cited instead and no EO 12977 text is relied on. Federal Register disposition notes for EO 10977 list 'Amended by: EO 11382', 'EO 13286' and 'See: EO 13154'; each is reconciled above. The Code (release point 119-121) records at 6 U.S.C. 111 note that section 72 of EO 13286 amended Ex. Ord. No. 10977 and prints no ending statement. The claim rests on the original-plus-bounded-search route: no held instrument or own term ends any clause, and the three bounded searches found no revocation or supersession.
